title: Membership of encoded pairs
statement: Let $f$ be a function on finite bit strings, let $z$ be a bit string, let $p$ be a natural number, and let $m$ be a Boolean mode. The Boolean indicator of the language defined by testing the output associated to $z$ at index $p$, on the encoded input consisting of $z$ and the binary representation of $p$, equals true exactly when $p$ is less than the associated output's length if $m$ is true; when $m$ is false, it equals the bit at position $p$ of that output, with out-of-range positions interpreted as false.
